hints: Focus on the reagent, hot concentrated NaOH in ethanol favours elimination of HX to form alkenes, not substitution.
Count the halogens in J, two Br plus one Cl means three molecules of HX can be lost, so three new C=C bonds are added to the one already present.
Check that the carbon skeleton cannot change, the gem-dimethyl group and the single methyl group must stay exactly where they are, and a C with no H cannot lose H.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Hot concentrated NaOH in ethanol causes dehydrohalogenation. Each C-Br or C-Cl loses $\text{HX}$ with a H from a neighbouring carbon to give a new C=C.

$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CHX-R} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH-R} + \text{X}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the molecular formula of X**

J is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{23}\text{Br}_2\text{Cl}$. Loss of $2\text{HBr} + \text{HCl}$ removes $3\text{H} + 2\text{Br} + \text{Cl}$.

$$\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{23}\text{Br}_2\text{Cl} - 3\text{H} - 2\text{Br} - \text{Cl} = \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}$$
This is a hydrocarbon. J already has one exocyclic $\text{C=CH}_2$, so X must have $1 + 3 = 4$ double bonds in total.

**Keep the carbon skeleton fixed**

Elimination does not move methyl groups. J has a $\text{C(CH}_3)_2$ gem-dimethyl on the left ring and a single $\text{C(CH}_3)$ on the right ring. X must show the same pattern.

**Check where double bonds can form**

On the left ring, Br is next to the $\text{C(CH}_3)_2$ carbon which has no H. So H can only be lost from the other side, giving $\text{C3=C4}$ away from the gem group. On the right ring, both the Br carbon and the Cl carbon have $\text{CH}_2$ neighbours with H, so two ring alkenes can form, one involving the $\text{C-CH}_3$ carbon. Only the structure with gem-dimethyl intact, single methyl intact, and four $\text{C=C}$ bonds fits all these rules.

options.A: Shows the unchanged spiro skeleton with $\text{C(CH}_3)_2$ on the left and $\text{CH}_3$ on the right. It has one left-ring alkene plus one exocyclic methylene plus a diene in the right ring, total four C=C bonds, matching $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}$ from loss of three HX.
options.B: Has four double bonds but the left ring shows only one methyl instead of gem-dimethyl. This would require breaking a C-C bond and moving a methyl group, which does not happen in elimination.
options.C: Has only one methyl on the left ring instead of the required gem-dimethyl, so the skeleton is changed. It also does not place the alkenes where H is available for elimination.
options.D: Keeps the methyl positions correctly but shows only three C=C bonds in total, one in the right ring instead of two. This corresponds to loss of only two HX, not the full elimination expected with excess hot ethanolic NaOH.
